title: Friction
seo_title: Year 5 Science: Friction Worksheets (Surfaces, Grip and Newton Meters)
standard_text: Identify the effects of air resistance, water resistance and friction, that act between moving surfaces.
meta_desc: Free Year 5 science worksheets on friction: which way friction acts, rough and smooth surfaces, helpful and unhelpful friction, and surface investigations with newton meters and ramps. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Rough surfaces grip and slow things; smooth or oiled surfaces slide.
body_html:
How to think about it

Friction is a force between surfaces that acts against movement.

  • Rough surfaces give more friction; smooth surfaces give less.
  • Friction helps us grip and stop (shoes, brakes, tyres) but can waste energy and wear things out (engines, chains).
  • Reduce it with oil, wheels and smooth surfaces; increase it with treads, grit and rubber.
Example

A box slides to the right. Friction acts?

Against the movement

Answer: to the left

Example

Carpet 9 N, ice 1 N. Most friction?

Bigger force needed

Answer: carpet

Common mistakes

  • Thinking friction acts in the direction of movement.
  • Thinking friction is always bad.
  • Thinking smooth surfaces have more friction.

faq.a: A force that acts between two surfaces that are moving, or trying to move, across each other. It always acts against the movement.
Both. It lets us walk, grip and stop with brakes, but it also slows machines down, wastes energy as heat and wears parts out.
Use oil or grease, wheels or ball bearings, or make the surfaces smoother.
